correctness.rationale: The exact unit-measure one-point example H1=H2=C, Fi=1, Gi=-1 gives each mixed quadratic form q_i(z)=-|z|^2, violating any positive biframe lower bound. Their tensors have G1 tensor G2=(+1) and F1 tensor F2=+1, so q_tensor(z tensor w)=|z|^2|w|^2, a Parseval biframe. This refutes the unrotated converse of the printed 2023 theorem without any measure-theoretic caveat. Under explicitly assumed Fubini product factorization, tensor inequalities imply q_i never vanish for nonzero arguments; fixing a unit g0 and setting ζ=q2(g0)/|q2(g0)| rotates ζ q1(f) onto the positive real axis with positive two-sided bounds, and fixing f0 similarly gives bounds for ζ^{-1}q2(g). Reciprocal phases cancel in the tensor; the converse follows by multiplying positive rotated bounds. The convention is the source convention that scaling the second vector by ζ scales the mixed form by ζ. No integrability claim beyond the stated hypotheses.
residual_risks: The phase-corrected equivalence requires existence of factor scalar integrals and valid product Fubini factorization, not asserted from weak measurability alone.
